key_insight: Introduce an on-policy adversarial flow distillation method that trains causal autoregressive student video models using only completed, prompt-conditioned videos from black-box teachers by matching transition flows under the student's own rollout distribution.
problem_solved: Enables distillation of powerful, potentially non-causal or black-box teachers into causal autoregressive students despite mismatch in architecture, temporal design, sampling schedule, and the teacher only providing finished videos—making off-policy supervised or score-based distillation ineffective.
method: On-policy student rollouts: generate trajectories from the student and compare transitions under the student's own distribution to avoid compounding prediction errors.
Adversarial flow matching: use a discriminator to measure and minimize the mismatch between the student's transition flows and teacher-conditioned flows inferred from completed teacher videos.
Black-box teacher interface: operate with only prompt-conditioned completed videos (no internal scores or schedules), robust to architecture and sampling differences.
impact: Makes it practical to compress and deploy strong video generators as causal, streaming-capable models that operate under their own rollouts—reducing error accumulation and enabling real-time or interactive applications.
